title: In the CODATA listing, 'exact' means no standard uncertainty is carried
summary: Defined constants and some conventional values are marked exact. Measured constants are printed with a standard uncertainty. The two marks are not the same kind of knowledge.
body: The NIST 2022 complete listing uses the word 'exact' on some lines and a standard uncertainty on others. Lines marked exact in the portion copied for this shard include the speed of light, the Planck constant, the elementary charge, the Boltzmann constant, the Avogadro constant, standard gravity, the standard atmosphere, and standard-state pressure. Lines printed with a standard uncertainty include G, the fine-structure constant, the electron mass, and the vacuum permittivity. BIPM says the seven defining constants have no uncertainty because their numerical values are fixed by the definitions. Standard gravity and the two standard pressures are also marked exact in the NIST listing, but they are conventional reference values, not members of BIPM's list of seven defining constants. 'Exact' in the listing is a statement about the table. It is not, by itself, a statement that a laboratory can realise the unit with zero error. BIPM separates definitions, which are fixed, from realisations, which are experimental.
